payload.text: Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery designed to suppress electrolyte crossover, a key aging mechanism in sodium-flow systems. The independently audited, governing cycle-life result is 8,400 cycles to the stated capacity threshold. The prototype’s gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg, while projected stack-level cost at 500 MWh manufacturing scale is $61/kWh. Its principal operational limitation is a 4 °C floor: below this temperature, the thalliline dopant precipitates from the negative electrolyte and cycling must stop.
